legacy_b002: Today I'm only selling. Usual prices. Nothing else.
legacy_b005: Then don't take them. It's not as if this is the only shop I can go to.
legacy_b006: The detective has started looking into my mother's case. He says the people behind it may be bigger than I thought.
Big enough that knowing the truth won't be enough.
Even if he finds out the truth, I'd need connections to get her out and capital to get back upstairs. I have neither.
...Don't answer that. I didn't come here to complain.
legacy_b008: I take back what I said that day. Once it's clear, I'll help you.
You said 'you'll do as I say from now on' and 'not just in business.' I heard you.
I was wrong. None of that counts. You can refuse what I say today and still keep investigating.
I can't repay a loan. I won't take charity.
Come work at the shop. Check stock, sort goods, run errands. Anything you can't handle, I'll find a way.
We'll take it one thing at a time. If I can't do it, I'll tell you first.
Fine. First tell me exactly what the work is. Don't think I've forgotten what you said that day.
legacy_b011: Then we'll try it. I do the work, and I'll be watching you keep your word.
When the detective has news, show me first.
Fine. I was wondering where to sort out what I've found.
legacy_b012: Hmph. You'd better not be testing whether I'd agree.
No. I was thinking too far ahead again.
At least you sound like a person this time. When the detective has news, I'll still come by.
legacy_b013: I was wrong that day. Arrange the investigation yourself. If you need help, come to me.
...At least you know how to apologize first.
That's the end of it. Say what you mean from now on. Don't make me guess what 'do as I say' includes.
Mm. If the detective has news, I'll come by.
m11_b001: Done! I've saved up the eight hundred for the detective. Counted three times. Not a credit short.
Including that thing I refused to admit was scrap. The parts from it sold for money, so don't look down on it.
m11_b002: I've got the detective's money. I sold the rest to another buyer, and the short-work people agreed to an advance.
I'll still work. The advance is paid, but the work won't finish itself.
m11_b003: I sold the locket too. Stop staring at my neckline. I'm still getting used to it myself.
I know who I sold it to. Mother comes first. I can't hold everything else back just because I'm reluctant.
m11_b004: The investigator starts tomorrow. He agreed to check the work records first, rather than question people at the company.
Once it's clear, I'll take it to court. Whether the court will look at it, I don't know.
I can't even get through the upper district gate, let alone hire a lawyer. None of my old friends will take my calls.
All I know is to keep investigating. Once it's clear, there will be a next step.
m11_b006: I can help with the next step. Work in the shop: check goods, keep accounts, run errands. I'll find a way for your mother's case too.
Do you really need the help, or are you just finding an excuse to give me money?
There's real work. If you do it badly, I'll still say so.
I can wipe the counter, and I'm learning the stock. But how far can you actually help?
Getting someone out takes paperwork. Getting things done takes knowing the right people. I've dealt with that. If I'm not sure, I won't promise.
'There's always a way.' I can say that myself. Don't use it to placate me.
I'll hear the terms first. If I refuse after hearing them, you don't get to turn cold. Keep buying from me as usual.
m11_b007: First, a time limit. You help me get back upstairs, and I work for you. I go back under my own name, not on someone's charity.
A pass isn't enough. If people keep me, it has to be because I'm good, not because of whose daughter I am.
My time for the case, short work and Mother is mine. If something comes up, I'll tell you. Don't expect me to drop everything when you call.
We decide together. You tell me every step.
Also, Mother and the research aren't part of the deal. Who gets the files and which road we take have to be decided together.
Don't tell me you've already decided what I should call you.
You choose what I call you.
I'll be watching. The day I think you're taking payment out of me, I'm gone. We can talk work. Keep the rest out of it.
m11_b008: I have one condition too. Eight hundred, as an advance on wages.
I said I don't want a handout—
This is an advance on wages, not charity. Your mother will need medicine and a place to stay when she's out. An advance before work starts - that's the rule.
You really know how to word things. I'm paying the detective myself. That's money I earned.
...Leave that stack here for now. If Mother needs it, I'll take it.
m11_b011: Set my work days first. If there's news about mother, I have to go.
See the detective first tomorrow. We'll schedule after we hear something.
This money is for her medicine and a place to stay. I'll find another way to cover the investigation.
I won't shirk the work. Don't just talk about what you promised me.
m11_b012: Let's leave it. Follow your own plan for the investigation.
You'd better not be testing whether I'll take the money.
You didn't overthink it. You're just provoking. If there's news tomorrow, I'll still come.
m12_b001: The detective found something. I read it all night. There are still things I can't make out.
I took a long way around and changed the handoff spot. Don't think you're the only one who knows to be careful.
Sit down first. I'll show you the parts I can't understand.
m12_b002: The drive was hidden in Mother's old laboratory. The investigator couldn't open it. There's a password.
The password is my birthday. She always said she'd never forget it. How many times did I tell her not to use that?
m12_b003: She found a way to make ordinary Nutrifruit produce seeds again. Plant it, harvest it, and keep seeds for the next crop.
This way we won't have to buy seeds from Pastel every time.
There are records here too... someone ordered her to stop the trial. Then her access was revoked. Then came the charge.
She never embezzled a single credit. She just touched the business Pastel was most afraid of losing.
This explains why they went after her. But getting them to release her will take another plan. At least this time I have more than 'my mother wouldn't do that.'
m12_b006: Leave the drive with me. I can watch the counter.
Fine. But I decide who it goes to.
Write me a receipt. I can come get it anytime, and you return it anytime.
m12_b007: Keep it on you. If someone comes asking, I'll stall them.
You'll use your shop to shield me? Fine. Then shield it to the end.
If anyone comes to you, tell me immediately, including what they offer. Don't make a deal and then expect me to go along.
m12_b008: Also, you've mixed several little components together. One of the labels has fallen off.
You spent ages inspecting my last lot. I wasn't only angry.
I separated them. The ones I'm not sure about are here for you to check.
m12_b009: This shell was replaced, but the price on the label wasn't changed.
You have to look inside too, right? A replaced shell doesn't always mean it's broken.
Right. Don't put it with the bad ones yet.
Then how do you inspect it? Tell me clearly. Next time I'll look myself.
m12_b004: Before we look at the drive, there's something else. When the man pretending to be your uncle brought that crate, I already knew something was wrong. I didn't warn you.
...You're telling me now? I thought I was just too stupid to see it.
I should have told you earlier. I'm sorry.
And after one apology, I'm supposed to take out the drive and follow your arrangements?
No. You can take it away.
If there's danger again, tell me first, no matter how bad it sounds. I'll decide whether I can take it.
m12_b005: I'll keep the drive. We can discuss what comes next. The shop agreement ends here.
Then remember that. Don't take it back someday.
m13_b001: Boss, you've been getting close to Eleanor lately. The girl from the Upper Level.
m13_b002: So you know I was taken away. Then you should understand I'm not here to make trouble for fun.
m13_b003: She has a data drive. Hand it over, and someone will tell you where to pick up her mother. She'll make it to the lower levels alive.
Deliver first, then wait for your address?
What else? Drag it out too long and her mother may not have that much time.
Three hundred if it works. You're a shopkeeper. Don't shut out your own payment.
Who releases her, and when can I see her? Say it clearly. I'll tell her about the three hundred too.
I hear she's working for you. If you tell her, she'll listen better than us.
Then pass it on quickly. Her mother can't wait.
m13_b006: I've got everything here. Just not what you're looking for.
m13_b007: Both of you will be on the record. Think carefully.
So will the message you brought.
m13_b008: Don't keep me waiting too long. My patience isn't that good.
m14_b001: What do we start with today? Those things you mentioned—
*tells her about the black-market visitor, including the three hundred*
m14_b002: Hand over the drive first, then they tell me where to pick her up... but at least they're willing to talk.
I'll go ask. If I can reach someone who can actually act—
With the drive, or with this paper?
Do you think I stop listening as soon as I'm anxious?
Once the drive is out of my hands, they make the rules. Find out where she's held, who's handling it, and where I can see her. If we ask wrong, we can still pull back.
What can I do now? Will sitting here get mother out?
Start with her medication records. Whoever received each dose signed for it. You know them. Leave the drive here.
All right, I'll handle that. If all I get back is 'wait a little longer,' we change approach.
m14_b003: There's a channel to apply for her transfer to protective custody. Submit the materials, find out who's responsible, then talk about going public.
I'll find her medication records. I have her identification too. I know what can't be left out.
m14_b004: I don't have a channel that guarantees her safety. For now, we talk about trading the drive for her release.
Then don't pretend it's arranged just to make me feel better. I'd rather hear the truth.
m14_b005: You promised to help me get back upstairs. Right now I just want to see her first.
Then do that first. I'll tell you exactly how far I can go.
Before it's done, don't tell me to 'relax.' I'm afraid I'll hold on to those words and wait forever.
Fine. When there's a result, we look at it together. This time we'll follow your lead.
m14_b007: Save your mother first. Hand the research back, but before you do, verify the release paperwork and where to pick her up.
All right. I won't gamble with her life.
If she asks later, I'll explain. You don't have to carry this alone.
m14_b008: Apply for protection first. Once she's safe, deal with the research. If protection falls through, switch back to trading the drive.
Understood. If it isn't settled, treat it as if it hasn't happened.
You used to say the same when buying from me. If it hasn't been inspected, don't put it in the price yet.
m14_b009: We can also go public now. But without protection, they really might kill her. I can't guarantee I can save her.
They will not even say where they would release her. Once I hand it over, all I have is their word. But publishing it now puts her at risk too...
I want her alive. And after everything she has endured, I want her work to survive too.
m14_b010: ...Send the research to the newspaper. At least they will not be able to take that copy back.
No. I do not know whether Mother would agree. This is my decision.
But do not tell me she will certainly be all right. I would believe you.
m14_b011: I've thought it through. I'm out of the investigation, and the shop agreement ends here. Here's the drive.
You promised me an Upper Level.
I know. That's why I'm saying it now, before I make a mess of it.
...Good. At least you didn't pretend you could carry it.
m14_b013: Leave today's shop work for now. Write down what you want to ask and go rest.
I can't get out of tomorrow's short shift. I'll bring the files, but I'll be late. I thought you'd say 'follow my schedule first' again.
I set my own time. You remember that too.
m15_b001: I brought the materials for getting Mother out. I've checked every page. The dates match.
You haven't eaten, have you? You said the same last time.
Look at the files first. Food can wait.
m15_b002: The medicine list checks out. But they changed the handoff location again.
I turned back halfway. The man said if I don't bring the drive, I won't see the next person.
I almost went. If you want to say 'I told you so,' go ahead.
You brought it back. We can still negotiate.
I found the original handler. He agreed to let me see the release paperwork without going through the messenger.
The handler, the time, the place - keep them separate. Once the handler is fixed, then we talk about when to hand over the drive.
...Go through it with me again. Especially the two steps he said we could skip.
m15_b003: I have all the protection application materials, but no one has been assigned to her care yet. I thought about sending the research out first so it wouldn't drag.
Once it's sent, who will wait for that confirmation on your behalf?
...Deliver first, then wait for someone else to speak. Again.
Put the medication list on top. I'll ask about the channel; you ask about the caregiver. Both sides have to match before it counts.
I made a separate copy of the medication she can't stop. If the caregiver can't answer for it, a notice won't be enough.
m15_b004: The protection route isn't done. No one can confirm they'll take over today.
The papers are ready, and it's still no?
So the research can't go out now. As agreed, switch to trading the drive and get the release paperwork clear first.
I don't like this way. But hearing it now is better than waiting blindly for news that never came.
m15_b005: Bought an extra portion. Pay for it normally. Don't say you'll add it to my wages.
Eat first. I'll use this corner to finish sorting the files.
m15_b006: You already checked this part. I know.
...I need you to look before I count on the next step. Just today.
m16_b001: I saw Mother! At the place we agreed on, and the handler hadn't been swapped.
Yes! I saw her first, checked her medication and the paperwork, and only then handed over the drive.
The messenger tried to lead me somewhere else again. I didn't follow. In the end he had to step aside.
You held them to what you'd checked.
...If I'd gone with the drive that day, I wouldn't even know who to ask now.
The first thing she asked was how much weight I'd lost. I had a whole speech ready, and she scattered it with one question.
m16_b002: They sent someone to the shop with those three hundred credits.
I returned it untouched. They wanted me to pressure you into handing over the drive. I didn't do their errand.
m16_b003: Mother's been moved out safely! I saw her, and the caregiver checked every item on the medication list.
None. When the application notice came first, I wanted to push you to send the research.
Later I asked and found out the pickup time had never been set. If I'd sent the research out first...
Because I read that notice one more time. ...I'll remember this time.
She complained my writing was too small. Nobody else would start with that.
Get her settled first. The research goes according to what we agreed.
m16_b004: I meant to come in, explain the paperwork properly, then discuss what comes next.
m16_b005: All the way back, I kept thinking what to tell you first.
m16_b006: Don't repeat what just happened to anyone.
Go back and stay with her. You don't have to work today. Come tomorrow if you want. Roll up those sleeves.
I know! I'll alter the clothes myself. Don't order anything for me first.
I'll ask Wilde about a place. You two need somewhere you can stay long-term.
She's out now. You're still taking care of the rest?
What I promised you wasn't just getting her out.
...I'll go home first. We'll talk about tomorrow, tomorrow.
m16_b007: And the box. I haven't forgotten.
This time you told me who came, what they said, which steps hadn't worked.
A few times I wanted to blame you for dragging it out, but in the end I kept coming back with you to look.
...Next time there's danger, tell me first. Don't wait for me to ask.
m17_b001: Hello. I've come for some household goods. Eleanor said not to choose the prettiest ones. Choose sturdy ones first.
Now she chooses for me, and complains that I'm too slow.
She's out handling something today. Before she left, she told me the way here twice.
m17_b003: She said she earned the investigation money herself. What you gave her was wages in advance.
m17_b004: She said she earned the investigation money herself. Later she came back and discussed the terms of your help properly.
m17_b005: She told me. Which days she comes, what you can't decide for her. She remembers clearly.
When she goes out now, she often says she'll ask the shopkeeper first. Then adds that something needs checking.
I asked her whether she's unsure about everything, or just needs someone to look it over with her before she feels safe.
She said I asked too many questions and went out for a walk. When she came back, she asked whether the shop still had work for her tomorrow.
Let her think about the rest herself. I've only just come back. I'm in no hurry to explain it for her.
m17_b006: It hurts to have given the research back. But she needn't explain herself every day for bringing me home.
She's afraid I'll be disappointed. Tell her for me: the lamp's bought but not installed yet. We're all here. Let's live the days in front of us first.
m17_b007: I'll keep following up on the review and the research. You've both done a great deal of running around for me.
She made a list of things to do. Your shop takes up several lines on it.
m17_b008: That's everything. Charge the usual price.
She specifically said not to mix the household accounts into her wages.
Since she was little she's liked to say she can count clearly. But when it's time to decide, she always stands in the doorway for ages.
You don't look like the type to rush her.
m18_b002: The altered clothes aren't ready. This will do today. I won't sweep anything off again.
Nothing happened with Mother today. I finished everything I could before coming.
I'm telling you first. So you don't send me home again.
m18_b003: I've checked these. Written down prices too.
...The moment you hold out your hand, I want to turn the labels over again.
They looked right when I calculated them myself.
Look if you want. Don't just pick faults. Check whether my math is right too.
m18_b004: My own goods first, then your work. Payment for goods and wages are separate.
I've put the damaged ones aside. Don't value them all together.
It's a fair price. You don't need to make it easy for me.
m18_b005: All right. About what I worked out.
m18_b006: If today isn't right, I'll ask elsewhere. I still agreed to do the work here, and I will.
m18_b007: I priced this too high. Saw the new casing, missed the wear inside.
The other sheet - the problems I found - also needs to go on the record.
The pen's right here. I'll get it myself.
m18_b008: Someone offered me a whole lot, cheaper. I was going to accept.
Now I want to bring it to you to look at together. ...If you're busy, I'll come back later.
First ask whether they'll let me inspect item by item, and record the prices.
I've noticed lately that whatever it is, I want to ask you first. This habit... I need to think about it.
m18_b009: And about the housing. Wilde's people came by.
The new place isn't big, but the light's bright enough to read, and Mother's things don't all have to be piled by the bed.
She told me to tell you: don't empty out the shop.
She also said your accounting is more presentable than when I first came. I'm delivering that word for word. I'm not responsible for explaining it.
m18_b010: I'll ask about that lot first. Bring the records next time.
If I'm not sure, I'll save it and ask you.
Don't think I have to ask about everything. I'm still learning to decide for myself.
m19_b001: Had the cuffs altered again. Tried inspecting and carrying things. They won't get in the way.
I asked about that lot. It can be inspected piece by piece. I asked properly, and they took two pieces and repriced.
The rest get the same inspection. I wrote my own price and didn't agree first.
m19_b002: There's something we need to settle first. That crate from the man pretending to be my uncle. You already knew something was wrong with it.
I know. I should have told you.
I remember what you did afterward. But don't use helping me, or the agreement, to cover this up.
I won't. I was wrong. I'm sorry.
...Tell me things first from now on. Even the ugly ones. I don't want to be the last person to know.
m19_b005: When you told me to hold on to the drive, I really thought of taking it myself.
After Mother got out, I thought I wouldn't have to come to you for everything anymore.
But the lot, those two labels...my first thought is still to bring them for you to check.
I didn't want you to do everything for me.
It's just... when you've decided, I can work steadily without worrying the whole time that I've missed something.
m19_b006: When we first talked about the agreement, what I couldn't stand most was that bossy tone of yours.
But there are things I want your judgment on first. Not because I took those wages.
m19_b007: Before, I could say I used that name because it was in the agreement.
I have to own this part myself now. There are things I want your judgment on first.
Don't look as though you knew all along.
m19_b008: I almost changed my wording again just now.
Leave today's things here for now.
m20_b001: Someone wants usable old equipment and materials. I said they could look here. Didn't promise stock or a discount.
Let him come himself. I just wanted to tell you first.
m20_b003: That customer I sent to buy used equipment. Did he come by?
I looked at the goods. We talked price. Don't recite the numbers. I'm asking how good my eye is!
m20_b004: If it didn't work out with that used-equipment buyer I sent, leave it. You don't have to sell to him just because I sent him.
m20_b005: Don't talk. Let me finish first, or I might not be able to say it.
m20_b006: After mother got out, I found plenty of reasons. Work here, learn the goods, repay what you'd done little by little.
But now that I know how to check goods, I still want to bring them to you. When nothing's happening, I wonder whether the shop is busy too.
I thought about that name all the way here last time. Then all the way home after saying it.
I want to hear your judgment. I want to look after things here. But I want more than doing the work well.
I want to be your lover. And stay here as the person you can call over, the one you can trust with things.
I've thought this through. You didn't decide it for me with that money.
m20_b008: I understand. Be my attendant, and my lover. Come here.
...You answered so quickly. I spent all night preparing, and I haven't finished.
I want to hold your hand.
m20_b009: Then hold it properly. Don't let go at the first crooked item.
That name is only for when we're alone.
Going back upstairs still counts. Don't think agreeing to be lovers lets you off the hook.
...Master. I'll follow your lead with today's work too.
m20_b010: I love you too. Let's end the agreement and just be lovers.
If you want to go back, you can do it under your own name. You don't need to work for it.
...You really do have faith in me.
Good. Then when I call you, don't pretend you didn't hear.
m20_b011: You're important to me. But I think we should stay friends.
Then the agreement ends here too. I don't want to serve as your attendant while pretending today never happened.
I'll handle going back upstairs myself. I know where to start now. Thank you for that.
I'll still come when I have goods. And still argue if the price is wrong.
m21_b001: I only came to buy something. But first I want to ask—does Eleanor really call you that?
A while ago I asked why she was in such a hurry. She said, "Master doesn't know I'm coming in late today."
Then she stopped short herself. And told me not to make a fuss.
m21_b002: She used to complain if someone carried her shopping bags at the wrong angle. Now she tells me you forget to eat and leave your pen everywhere.
She still picks faults. But after she picks them, she actually does something about them.
m21_b003: I asked whether she'd still not paid off that money. She said it was wages, not a loan, and told me not to turn everything into a debt.
m21_b004: I asked whether she owed you something. She said no. She'd come back later and renegotiated every term herself.
m21_b005: I asked someone who knows jewelry about that bracelet. The price you offered was fair.
She looked prouder hearing me admit that than she does when someone praises her.
m21_b006: People upstairs are already talking. Saying she's down here, working as a pawnbroker's maid.
That she's dating the owner too. Telling half a story and leaving half out just sounds spiteful.
They reacted about the same as I did when I first heard. You can be a little smug. Just not this obviously.
But seriously. She wants to get back on her own. When that day comes, someone will throw it in her face.
I think she's ready. You sound more sure of it than she does.
m21_b007: That's everything. Don't quote me some incomprehensible price just because I know your attendant.
I know. She told the regulars to charge me normally.
...She really does speak for you now.
m22_b001: Mother's found a little work. Growing things. Nothing large, but she's taking it very seriously.
I'll help. But she won't let me hover all day. Says if I stand there, I can't help picking at her mistakes.
m22_b002: There's news about the research on making Nutrifruit seed again. That doesn't mean everyone will be eating their own crop tomorrow. There are trials to run, and people willing to run them.
Mother's busy cooperating with the review, and explaining the materials to everyone who received them, over and over. Now she complains every day isn't long enough.
m22_b003: Lydia says she can find me a position upstairs. I asked what it was. She said, first there's a place, the details later.
I'm not going. I don't want an empty position. I want them to remember me.
I know she means well. But I don't want to sit in a job nobody can explain, waiting every month for pay that comes because of her.
An introduction isn't a bad thing. If she finds people willing to look at samples, I'll go. But next time they should come to me because the goods are good and the deliveries are on time.
We agreed it would be under my own name.
...So the half you promised me is still owed.
m22_b004: Lydia really did come ask you last time.
I knew it. When it slipped out, she looked as if I'd lost the entire Upper Level to you.
I told her you explain things clearly when teaching me goods, and when someone threatened me, you didn't push me out. As for why I like you—she doesn't need a report to believe that.
She asked whether I said you're annoying. I said yes. That was the part she listened to most carefully.
m22_b005: And this. I've always worn it. I want you to have it.
The pendant Mother gave me. She knows. She said don't come back someday saying I never thought it through.
I've thought it through. Now she can say my name herself. I want to leave this with the other person who'll wait for me to come back.
m22_b006: Don't mix it in with the goods for sale. This one has no price tag.
m22_b007: Keep wearing it. I'll remember what you meant.
All right. Then every time you see it, remember. Don't pretend I never offered.
m22_b008: I've thought about finding the locket again. I haven't yet.
No rush. It's not like I need to hand over an object before I can make myself clear.
m23_b001: No news from the investigation today. Nobody sent me with terms either.
To see my master. Do I need a reason?
Hmph. I'm not this free every day.
m23_b002: You still arrange so many things badly here.
I was the one who said a place like this doesn't count as a shop. How many times do you want me to admit it?
It still isn't pretty. Same lamp. Same corner of the counter that catches my sleeve.
But I still come. My master is here. Am I supposed to go wipe counters in someone else's shop?
m23_b003: I saved this for you. Perfume. It refills itself. Don't smell it and immediately ask what it sells for.
When I want to smell it, I can come find you.
m23_b005: I'll keep an eye on the scavenging sites too. I know a few places with things left, and a few people whose word isn't worth much.
I wanted to save you some wrong turns, not have you wash your hands of it!
m23_b006: Almost forgot. Mother's review materials were formally submitted.
This time they gave a receipt. Investigation report, transfer record, research receipt. Nothing missing.
I made them write the dates clearly in front of me, so next time they can't say they can't find them.
Mother's name can't rest on someone's verbal promise.
m23_b007: ...I can't tell whether what comes next is work or something else.
m23_b009: One more thing. If I don't say it today, I'll put it off again.
I want the people upstairs to see it clearly - I learned to judge stock, negotiate, and earn my own meals down here. I'll walk back under my own name. No hiding from anyone, and no hiding you.
Wilde has a list for the half you promised me.
...I'll do my part properly. Don't ruin the shop trying to hurry yours.
I don't want to end up supporting you one day.
m23_b010: Until that day comes, I'm still your attendant. So you'd better keep owing me.
m24_b001: Don't look at me like that! I just used the pass Wilde arranged to go upstairs, and I came down without changing.
This is made to upper-district rules. The cufflinks and the collar height. Nothing can be off.
I used to have a whole row of clothes like this. Now there's just this one. I can't even sit carelessly.
I'll go in first. You look at the stock. I'll tell you the rest later.
m24_b002: The inspector went through my papers for ages, then looked up and asked, 'You're the daughter from the embezzlement case?'
I said my name was Eleanor. It was on the documents.
Then he asked, 'I hear you're working as a pawnbroker's maid down below?'
Someone nearby laughed. A man who used to come to our house for dinner. I called him uncle when I was little.
The funniest part is, I wasn't nervous at all.
Standing there, I thought of the way you inspect stock. Other people can talk all they want; you look at the goods. If they're sound, you don't have to answer the talk.
m24_b003: The contact you arranged submitted the papers the day before. He noted who handled every step.
When the inspector saw who had handled it, his expression changed and he flipped through the rest in a hurry.
Your contact said, 'When the pawnshop owner asks, nobody in the lower district wants to botch it.'
...How many favors do you owe down here, and how many do you have saved up?
m24_b004: Everything went through normal procedure. Every page stamped. Every fee itemized.
He went back and forth, couldn't find a single fault, and finally had to push my papers back.
When the goods are sound, you can stand firm on the price. Turns out paperwork is the same.
m24_b005: In the end he only said, 'You can go, Miss Eleanor.'
He pushed the papers to the window and went to call the next person. I picked them up and walked through myself.
Only when the gate clicked behind me did I notice how tightly I was clutching the papers.
I remembered that inspector. I won't take anything from him again.
That walk was long. I never used to think it was that long.
Someone recognized me and asked about Mother first, then how I make a living. I said I work in the lower district. The owner knows goods, and his accounts are cleaner than theirs.
m24_b006: Mother still can't go back. I asked very carefully. Reviewing my pass doesn't revoke her exile.
She says it's enough for me to go and do what I need to. I shouldn't stop my own life waiting for hers.
m24_b007: Mother's case is still under review. When people ask, I only tell them what's confirmed. I haven't promised the rest in advance.
m24_b008: I brought Mother's formal notice too. If anyone asks, I show them. Her innocence has been established. My business is still mine to build.
m24_b009: The pass has my name on it. But the agreement - not yet.
The papers say me. But the names they use are still 'that case's daughter' and 'the pawnshop attendant.'
Getting the pass isn't the end. When they talk about me, I want them to say 'Eleanor.'
So I'll keep at it. ...You're still owing me.
m24_b010: Master, tell me. Do I look better in this, or the other outfit?
This one is for the people upstairs. That one is for me.
m25_b001: Don't speak yet. Look at this.
m25_b002: The sample for my first order. A household upstairs is renovating its growing room. They want reliable used equipment and materials.
New goods are too expensive, and they don't dare buy old ones. Upstairs, people assume nine out of ten things from the lower district are stolen.
Where it came from, its condition, what was repaired, what was replaced—it's all on the label. I remember which scrap field each piece came from.
Goods come from below, get inspected below, and sell above. You have to know both ends.
I'm not charging extra for this sample. Buy it at the usual price. The lot beside it is separate. If you want in, we'll talk.
m25_b003: I've waited a long time to hear that.
I'm proud of myself now. You're not allowed to say anything.
m25_b004: Before delivery, someone told that household my goods were stolen stock from a pawnshop.
An upper-district trading house that's dealt in secondhand goods for years.
The family came to ask me. I laid out the provenance record for every piece and showed them page by page.
Finally they asked the dealer: can you produce records like these for your own goods?
I signed the contract. My own name.
m25_b005: The person who introduced me came out of regard for you. He said, 'People upstairs have heard about that pawnbroker's eye too.'
m25_b006: You paid for the training, samples, trial work—all of it. They tested the sample several times before agreeing on a delivery date.
m25_b007: It's all ordinary equipment and existing seeds. Nothing from the research we returned. I did use everything Mother taught me about the basics.
m25_b008: The public research trials asked about procurement too. I inspect and supply goods. I won't write Mother's research down as mine.
m25_b009: Not just the training. The second time I brought goods, I insisted on quoting first. Two right, one uncertain, and someone wanted to charge tuition after the fact. I remember.
So half this order is yours.
I said half is half! ...Is it so hard to praise me, Master?
m26_b001: This is the pawnshop? Smaller than I expected.
I'm here to do business. A new supplier called Eleanor has appeared upstairs. Clean goods, complete records, fair prices. Several of us are asking where her stock comes from.
And every line of inquiry leads to you.
I'd like to deal directly with you. You supply, I buy. No need for her in the middle.
You're just a pawnshop owner. How much do you get from her? I'll pay you double.
m26_b003: My goods sell at my prices. Her business isn't mine to sell.
Not for ten times as much.
m26_b004: If you want her goods, speak to her. This shop is only one end of her route.
What if she won't lower her price?
m26_b005: I went to her first. I told her if she wouldn't lower her price, I'd go around her and deal with the person below her.
She said, 'Go ahead. He won't go around me.'
I thought she was bluffing. Now it looks like inspection and delivery still have to go through her. You two being tied together saves trouble.
Today, consider me a customer. Quote your usual prices.
m26_b007: Next time I go up, I will discuss delivery with her. For a large order, we will still have to negotiate the price.
One more thing, boss. When she introduces her supplier, she never says 'some pawnshop downstairs.' She says 'someone I trust.'
m27_b002: It's over! The showcase Wilde helped arrange finished today.
So many people came. More than I expected.
Samples in front, records beside them. Some people walked in, looked at the clothes and jewelry first, then glanced back at the records.
Afterward, some stayed asking questions until the end. When could the next batch arrive? Could we sign a long-term contract?
m27_b003: Mother came. She can go upstairs now.
When the formal notice came, she stared at it for a long time. She looked at it again before leaving today.
She stood in the last row and listened to everything. I got one number wrong and she frowned from the back. ...Just like at the farm.
m27_b004: Mother didn't come. The formal result isn't out yet, and she doesn't want to stand in public until the case is closed.
I rehearsed it with her last night. She found three things wrong. Today, wouldn't you know it, people asked about all three. Once the notice comes, I'll take her to see it.
m27_b005: Mother still can't go upstairs. The night before, she made me rehearse it in our room and found three weak points.
People asked about all three today.
m27_b006: Then someone came to me. One of the largest purchasing houses upstairs. The manager came himself.
The contract he offered was bigger than all my current orders combined.
You can guess the condition. Strike the pawnshop in the lower district from the supply and partner list. The people upstairs don't like pawnshops, and there are ugly rumors besides.
...Just like Lydia at the beginning. Back then it was 'stop mentioning your mother's case.' Today it's 'stop mentioning that pawnshop.'
In front of everyone I said, 'Where my goods come from, who inspects them, who put up the first capital—not one word comes off that list. If you object to pawnshops, find someone else to talk to.'
Then someone in the back walked up and said he'd sign. A moment later, a second person came.
When that manager left, his face looked worse than mine after my first Nutrifruit.
m27_b007: Half the people came through your connections. Someone told me they were there to show support for that shopkeeper.
I told them I didn't need a cheering section. Since they'd come, they should look at the goods.
m27_b008: Someone asked whether the supply was reliable. I said half the scavengers and owners downstairs knew my mas... my business partner.
...I changed what I called you. Of everyone there, only Lydia laughed out loud.
m27_b009: The venue, the samples, the arrangements. You spared none of it. Nobody could claim this presentation only succeeded through someone else's influence.
m27_b010: Lydia was there too. Afterward she came running over, but the first thing she said wasn't praise.
'They kept calling you by your name.'
Only then did I realize. Not once all day did anyone call me 'the daughter from that case.'
m27_b011: Next time, I will. I set the terms. I should be the one to say when they're fulfilled.
Today I need to go home and change first.
Change into which one? ...What do you think?
m28_b002: There is something to settle today. Afterwards, I want to spend a little longer here.
Do you remember the condition I set? Waiting for you to walk back into the upper district under your own name.
That day came. They remember Eleanor now, and they trust me with their business.
You did what you promised, and I finished the work I promised. That agreement ends today.
Who said I'm leaving? Someone upstairs asked me to dinner to discuss next quarter's order. I made them reschedule.
Because I made plans with you today. ...This outfit doesn't count as work anymore.
To see you. Before, I wanted to stay a little longer after work. Now I have my own business, and I still want to come.
Outside, people wait for me to speak. Back here, I still want to ask you first.
...Must I say what I call you as well?
m28_b003: The old agreement has ended. That name has not. Did you hear me?
m28_b005: Then let's make a new agreement. No end date this time.
First, don't use that name to tease me in front of customers. That hasn't changed.
Second, don't decide my affairs upstairs for me. I'll manage yours down here, until you're sick of it.
We decide together. I'm not unreasonable.
Third, eat every day. I'll check.
No time limit. You said that yourself.
m28_b006: I hear you. Come here, my lady.
...Never mind. A little closer is possible.
m28_b007: Since it's your choice, I'll take that 'master' to heart.
Then remember it. When someone's around, you call me by name.
m28_b008: This time, I decided. Nobody can change that. Not even you.
m28_b010: People say I'm harder to get hold of than I used to be.
With other people, yes. When you call, I come.
world_b003: The embezzlement conviction of the former head of the station's largest hydroponics farm has been formally overturned on review. Related charges and procedural issues will be investigated separately.
Trial planting of self-seeding Nutrifruit continues. The researchers say trial records will remain open for verification.
world_b004: We've got the official notice overturning Mother's conviction. She looked at her name first, then read the last line again.
She didn't say anything. After a long while, she said she wanted to cook a proper meal that evening. When she went to get the bowls, she took three.
She told me to tell you: don't bring anything. Just come.
world_b005: Next time I'll take her up to see the showroom. No business dinner. I just want her to see what I've made of it.
wait_b001: Don't rush this by handing over money the shop still needs.
If you're short, save up slowly. I never said it had to be done tomorrow.
...I can wait. The agreement has no date on it.
wait_b002: Still haven't secured that discount Wilde mentioned?
You still need the people over there to know you better. If we do it now, it's full price.
Save where you can. If you want to go ahead, paying full price is fine too. Don't stretch yourself too thin.
wait_b003: While you're getting things ready, I've gone over what I can do too. I'm not leaving all the work to you.
I haven't been idle. It's not like you bought a pretty vase to sit on a shelf.
...I am pretty, though. Wait until I finish this one, then we'll talk.
daily_b002: Retrieved it from where you put it. The wrong place. Second time now.
If I don't, Master will spend all his searching time asking me.
...If you want to talk to me, say so. Don't use misplaced things as an excuse.
daily_b003: Brought some food. Don't ask what it cost. I keep track of my own spending.
I used to turn my nose up at this stuff. I still do. This place just makes it edible.
This is the best I've picked! Do you know how long I spent choosing?
Tell me after you eat. Should I bring it again next time?
daily_b004: Someone at the door asked whether I worked here.
Yes. Then he asked whether I helped people like this upstairs too.
I got a little angry. So I told him: I only do this for my master. Anyone else could offer any amount and I wouldn't go.
Didn't we agree it's only for private? Don't use it to tease people. If I want to say it myself, that's different.
...That last part made even me a little embarrassed.
daily_b005: Looks quite tidy today. Nothing for me to do?
There is. Stay with me a while.
daily_b006: Master. You assigned the duty. Don't call someone over and then ignore her.
tragic_b002: The Nutrifruit research is with the newspaper. They've confirmed they can read it. They'll keep checking it.
Still no word about Mother. I went and asked.
Let me do something today. Otherwise I'll sit here wondering whether the news would come if I just waited a little longer.
Give me something to do. Put the checked orders together. Don't worry about the rest.
tragic_b004: Mother was killed. ...The news is true.
Don't tell me we did everything we could. I can't hear that right now.
All right. Sit for a while if you want.
Your half of the promise... the Upper Level...
It's your wages. I remember the work you did in the shop.
tragic_b005: But everything you did for me—
Doesn't become a debt. Look after yourself today.
tragic_b006: I've got a few of Mother's things back. I meant to sort them. Once I opened them up, I didn't know what to pick up first.
I used to be afraid of having no money, no news. Now there's nothing left to be afraid of, and I don't feel any lighter.
tragic_b007: I'll keep this for now. I don't want to give it away or sell it today.
tragic_b008: I used to think, once she was out, I'd ask her to come find the locket with me.
When you want to go, I'll come ask with you.
tragic_b009: I've decided to join the revolutionaries.
Not everything. But I can't just wait until someone else is taken like that, then start counting money again.
Write down where you're going and who you can reach. Don't follow anyone just because they say something nice.
I will. I haven't forgotten everything you taught me.
tragic_b010: I need a weapon that works. Something reliable. No display piece.
If I have one, I'll show you. If I don't, I won't pass off something broken.
All right. We judge the goods.
tragic_b012: Don't rush to calculate the rest. The rest... I can't make sense of it now either.
tragic_b013: Eleanor told me. She's leaving with the revolutionaries. I couldn't talk her out of it.
This time I heard her out. She also said the shop agreement is over. Nobody owes anybody.
She told me not to come here and argue on her behalf. ...Did I always make people feel I'd make things worse as soon as I spoke?
This time I'll listen to her.
tragic_b014: I'm about to leave with the Revolution, and I'm still thinking that if not for all this, I'd probably be here picking faults with how you arrange your stock.
...I'll remember all of this, no matter what happens after.
Come back when you have the chance.
All right. But don't wait for a date I can't promise.
tragic_b015: I'm here for the last few things. Once I leave with the revolutionaries, I won't be coming by so often.
tragic_b016: Keep the perfume. When you smell it, don't only remember me at my worst.
I remember your first time wiping the counter. You said the cloth was too rough.
You too. Don't get so busy you forget to eat.
exit_b002: I said it: the day I think you're taking payment out of me, I'm gone.
You don't want to talk about the crate again. I can't pretend it never happened. This ends here.
exit_b005: You handed over Mother's research disk?
Where's Mother? Did you see the release papers?
exit_b006: I didn't ask how much you got. I asked where she is!
On the first day I told you. Mother and the research were outside the agreement.
I did the work we agreed on. I told you everything I knew and waited for you to find out the truth. You promised to tell me when there was danger. Why was this the one thing that didn't count?
Don't call me back here. I'm done working in this place.
exit_b008: I heard it from someone else. You've already published the research.
My mother has no protection yet. You knew. So did I.
So you wanted me to tell you everything, while you said nothing yourself.
The agreement ends here. From now on, what I do is none of your business.
